findings.title: ADR-0024 (service drivers): exported Config.Validate validates against the host GOOS, not a target
findings.description: The ADR states as a rule that `Config.Validate` checks the rules of the target GOOS, not of the host, and as a consequence that "`Validate` has no host dependence. The same `Config` gives the same violations on every host". The exported method takes no GOOS and hard-wires runtime.GOOS; only the unexported validate(goos), reached through New with WithGOOS, follows a target. A caller of the public Validate therefore gets host-dependent results, which is exactly what the ADR says cannot happen.
findings.evidence: config.go:68-73: `// Validate reports every way c is unusable on runtime.GOOS ...` / `func (c Config) Validate() error { return c.validate(runtime.GOOS) }`. validate sets `windows := goos == "windows"` and checks `isAbs(c.Binary, windows)` (config.go:101), where isAbs for non-windows is `strings.HasPrefix(p, "/")`. So `service.Config{Name: ..., Binary: `C:\svc\tool.exe`, ...}.Validate()` reports "Binary ... is not an absolute path on linux" on a Linux host and nil on a Windows host; `Binary: "/usr/bin/tool"` is the reverse.
findings.suggestion: Either reword the ADR rule and consequence to say that validation inside New follows the WithGOOS target while the exported Validate uses runtime.GOOS, or give Validate a target (e.g. a ValidateFor(goos) method) so the ADR's claim holds for the public API.

findings.title: ADR-0024 (service drivers): the Windows service control manager driver the ADR describes does not exist
findings.description: The ADR says the service package "fronts the operating system's service manager (systemd, launchd, the Windows service control manager) behind one Manager interface" and that in New "A `case` per operating system returns that operating system's Driver". ADR-0028 (driver settings) and ADR-0029 (container) repeat the three-driver framing ("two of three operating systems", "Three copies of the check"). The code has two drivers; the windows case exists only to return ErrUnsupported.
findings.evidence: manager.go:47-49: "The drivers are systemd on linux and launchd on darwin; every other GOOS, windows included, has none." manager.go:106-107: `case "windows": return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrUnsupported, goos)`. `service.New(cfg, service.WithGOOS("windows"))` with a valid Config returns ErrUnsupported; no file in source/daemon/service implements a Windows driver (ls shows only systemd*.go and launchd*.go).
findings.suggestion: State in ADR-0024 that the Windows driver is not implemented and that New returns ErrUnsupported for windows (validation of a Windows Config still runs), or implement the driver.

findings.title: ADR-0029 (preflight): claims the updatetest release binary is a unix-only shell script and that Windows execution is untested
findings.description: The ADR says the binary of updatetest.NewRelease "is a `#!/bin/sh` script ... It is unix-only", that "Execution on Windows is not tested here; it is left to issue #60", and as a consequence that "`updatetest` releases need a shell. A test of a consumer that runs on Windows has to supply its own binary." None of that holds: on Windows NewRelease packs a Go program built at test time, and the preflight's real execution runs on the gated windows-latest job. The ADR's status line does not mark these statements as amended (ADR-0031 does not mention the test kit either).
findings.evidence: updatetest/server.go:120-130: `func ReleaseExecutable(t testing.TB, tag string) []byte` ... "[releaseScript] for any goos but \"windows\", the Go program of [releaseProgramSource] built for the target on \"windows\""; updatetest/program.go:54 runs `go build` for it. source/update/AGENTS.md: "The Windows job runs the preflight's real execution of a staged `.exe` ... so `TestApplyRunsTheStagedBinary` and `updatecmd`'s install tests run there too." .github/workflows/ci-test.yml:90-118 runs `go test -race -shuffle=on ./...` on windows-latest for update (it holds install_windows_test.go).
findings.suggestion: Update the `updatetest` rule and the two Windows consequences in ADR-0029 (or add an "amended by" note) to say the release binary is ReleaseExecutable: the shell script off Windows, a Go program built with the go command on Windows, and that Windows execution is covered by the test-windows job.

findings.title: ADR-0021 (extraction): names asset.DefaultExt, a tar.gz-only default and a CreateTemp pattern the code no longer has
findings.description: Three concrete claims of the ADR are contradicted by the code, and its status line ("extends ADR-0020") records no amendment: (1) "An empty template or extension counts as `asset.DefaultTemplate` or `asset.DefaultExt`" - there is no asset.DefaultExt; the default is the function asset.DefaultExtFor(goos). (2) "An empty `AssetExt` resolves to `tar.gz`, as every empty field resolves to its default" - it resolves to zip when the resolved GOOS is windows. (3) "The file is created there with `os.CreateTemp(dir, TempPrefix+\"*\")`" - the pattern carries the binary's extension. ADR-0031 lists only ADR-0022 and ADR-0023 as extended, so a reader of ADR-0021 is not pointed at the change.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "DefaultExt\b" source/update --include=*.go` finds only DefaultExtFor: asset/asset.go:64 `func DefaultExtFor(goos string) string { if goos == "windows" { return extZip ...`. config.go:515-516: `if r.AssetExt == "" { r.AssetExt = asset.DefaultExtFor(r.GOOS) }`, so `Config{GOOS: "windows", ...}` with an empty AssetExt extracts as zip, not tar.gz. extract.go:138: `f, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, r.TempPrefix+"*"+filepath.Ext(binaryFileName(r)))`, so a Windows target stages `<prefix><random>.exe`.
findings.suggestion: Amend ADR-0021 (or add "amended by ADR-0029 and ADR-0031" to its status) so the format rule names asset.DefaultExtFor(GOOS), the considered option says an empty AssetExt resolves to the per-GOOS default, and the staged-file rule gives the pattern TempPrefix+"*"+ext.

findings.title: ADR-0017 and ADR-0021 (completion installer) name cli/core's internal/atomicfile, which does not exist
findings.description: ADR-0017 says a valid edit "is chmodded 0600 and renamed over the file by `internal/atomicfile`", and ADR-0021 (completion installer) justifies its own atomic writer with "`cli/core`'s `internal/atomicfile` cannot be imported from `cli/spec`". cli/core has no such package: `config edit` uses go.vipengele.org/cli/state. Neither ADR's status line records the change (ADR-0018 state store explains it only from its own side).
findings.evidence: `ls source/cli/core/internal` -> `cobra errrender`; `grep -rn atomicfile source --include=*.go` finds nothing. edit.go:119 `if err := state.Replace(temp, opts.Path, editMode); err != nil {` and edit.go:143 `state.WriteFile(temp, data, editMode)`.
findings.suggestion: Replace the `internal/atomicfile` references with `cli/state` (Replace / WriteFile), or annotate both ADRs as amended by ADR-0018 (state store). In ADR-0021 the rationale for a private writer in completioninstall should then be restated (cli/spec does not require cli/state).

findings.title: ADR-0019 (filelock): golang.org/x/sys is not a direct requirement of filelock only, nor does it reach consumers through filelock alone
findings.description: The ADR decides "`golang.org/x/sys` is a direct requirement of this project only" and lists as a consequence "`golang.org/x/sys` enters a consumer's graph through `filelock` alone; `cli/state`, `cli/spec` and `commons` keep their dependency sets". update now requires x/sys directly (its installscript tests import it), and cli/spec already carries x/sys in its module graph through golang.org/x/term, independently of filelock.
findings.evidence: source/update/go.mod:13 `golang.org/x/sys v0.50.0` in the direct require block (no `// indirect`); imports at update/installscript/harness_pty_linux_test.go:10 (`golang.org/x/sys/unix`) and script_windows_test.go:15 (`golang.org/x/sys/windows/registry`). source/cli/spec/go.mod:8,11: `golang.org/x/term v0.47.0` direct and `golang.org/x/sys v0.49.0 // indirect`, while cli/spec does not require filelock.
findings.suggestion: Reword the decision to say filelock is the only project whose production code calls x/sys, and drop or qualify the "through filelock alone" consequence (cli/spec has it via x/term; update requires it for tests).

findings.title: ADR-0018 (state store) and ADR-0017 say a new project needs a Worker deploy before its first tag
findings.description: ADR-0018 (state store) lists as a consequence that `cli/state` "needs a Worker deploy before its first tag", and ADR-0017 counts "a Worker deploy" among the costs of a new project. The Worker reads its module list from the R2 object modules.json, which publish-vanity-modules.yml writes from source/**/go.mod on merge to main; a new project needs no Worker deploy, and a tools/vanity-worker tag deploys Worker code only. The sibling ADR-0019 (filelock) already states the current mechanism, so the two ADRs disagree with each other and with tools/ and .github/.
findings.evidence: docs/adr/0016-the-vanity-module-list-is-published-as-data-to-r2-from-main.md:17 ("The object `modules.json` in a Cloudflare R2 bucket ...") and :39 ("A `tools/vanity-worker/v*` tag deploys the Worker's code"); tools/vanity-worker/src/index.ts:48 reads the `MODULE_LIST` bucket; ADR-0019 filelock line 67-68: "resolves through `go.vipengele.org` once `publish-vanity-modules.yml` has run (ADR-0001, ADR-0016)".
findings.suggestion: Change both sentences to "resolves through go.vipengele.org once publish-vanity-modules.yml has run (ADR-0016)", as ADR-0019 (filelock) words it.

findings.title: ADR-0021 (completion installer): says the update project imports nothing of completioninstall in non-test code
findings.description: The ADR says "The `update` project holds the hook that calls it, and imports nothing of it" and "`update` does not import `completioninstall` in non-test code; its `example_test.go` wires the two together", and that "The full `install.sh` is out of scope; a tool embeds the snippet in its own". The update project's production package installscript imports completioninstall and renders the full install script around its snippet. ADR-0023 (install script) declares that it reconciles this, but ADR-0021's own status line carries no "amended by" note, so read alone it contradicts the code; the claim now holds only for the root package `update`.
findings.evidence: source/update/installscript/render.go:9 `"go.vipengele.org/cli/spec/completioninstall"` and :114 `snippet, err := completioninstall.Snippet(r.BinaryName)` in non-test code of module go.vipengele.org/update. source/update/AGENTS.md: "Package `update` does not import `cli/spec/completioninstall` outside tests (ADR-0021); `installscript` is the package that does (ADR-0023)."
findings.suggestion: Add "amended by ADR-0023 and ADR-0031" to ADR-0021's status and narrow the two sentences to the root package `update`.
